name_reason: Compliant with fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> (battle AI domain). Accurately describes the function: scores one (spell, candidate-tile) pair by summing per-target priority over the AoE target list. No Ghidra address residue in the name.
purpose: Enemy-AI per-candidate spell scorer: given a spell and the list of runtime_char indices it would affect, returns an aggregate priority score, dispatching the scoring rule by spell_id range (damage / heal / buff / status-inflict / cure).
logic_summary: score=0; pSpell=spell_effect_entry(spell_id); base_damage=*(u16*)pSpell. If spell_id<0xD: per target +0x18 if HP<base_damage (kill) else +8; for spell_id 10..12 first skip targets passing fd2_check_char_status_immunity (terrain-immune); if target.bChar_id==0 multiply that target's score by float10 const @0x50144 (priority-enemy boost, rounded via __CHP/FISTP). Else if spell_id<0x11 (heal 0xD..0x10): per target +8 if HP<max/3, +3 if HP<max/2, else +0; double if combat_aux[0x0D]&1 (heal-boost). Else if spell_id<0x14 (buff 0x11..0x13): score=tally_chars_with_zero_at_field(n, buf, spell_id+0x11, 3) -- count targets whose buff byte is still 0. Else exact spell_id: 0x14 +6 per target with poison flag (+0x25)!=0; 0x15 +6 per target with sleep/paralysis flag (+0x26)!=0; 0x16 +6 per target with silence flag (+0x27)==0 AND fd2_build_usable_spell_list!=0; 0x1A score=tally(...,0x25,4); 0x1B score=tally(...,0x26,4); any other id returns 0. runtime_char addr = idx*0x50 + data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr.
signature: int __cdecl fd2_score_spell_candidate(uint32 spell_id, uint32 n_targets, uint32 target_array_ptr)

params.name: spell_id
params.semantics: Spell id 0x00-0x23 being evaluated; selects the scoring dispatch branch. Passed by caller as (uint32)spell_list[spell_i]. In src signature the name is spell_id; Ghidra decompile shows param_1.
params.reason: Ghidra storage name is param_1 (generic placeholder); src already uses spell_id. Rename param_1->spell_id in Ghidra in Stage 2 to match src. No address residue, just a placeholder name.

params.name: n_targets
params.semantics: Count of entries in target_array_ptr (number of runtime_char indices the spell's AoE would affect at this candidate tile). Loop bound. Caller passes (uint32)n_targets from fd2_compute_aoe_targets.
params.reason: Ghidra storage name is param_2; src uses n_targets. Stage-2 rename param_2->n_targets. Placeholder, not address residue.

params.name: target_array_ptr
params.semantics: Pointer (as uint32) to a byte array of runtime_char indices (the AoE target ids). Indexed as *(uint8*)(i + target_array_ptr). Caller passes (uint32)tgt_buf.
params.reason: Ghidra storage name is param_3; src uses target_array_ptr. Stage-2 rename param_3->target_array_ptr. Placeholder, not address residue.

returns.semantics: Aggregate priority score for this (spell, candidate-tile) pair; higher = more desirable. Caller (fd2_ai_score_offensive_spell) compares it against data_fd2_battle_ai_best_spell_score (signed) and keeps the best. Returns 0 for spell ids this scorer does not handle.

comment_original_issue: src comment line listed '0x15 cure sleep' and '0x1A/0x1B summon (tally with 0x25/0x26)'. Per spell name table, 0x1A=毒擊術 (poison-strike) and 0x1B=麻痹術 (paralysis) are offensive status-inflict spells (the actual summon spells are 0x20-0x23, which this scorer does not handle), and 0x15=祛麻術 (cure paralysis). The 'summon' label was wrong and 'cure sleep' was imprecise.
notes: Logic verified against decompile + full disassembly (0x15b77-0x15da1); not re-validating equivalence, only confirming naming/comments. Two comment-semantic corrections applied (src + plate): 0x1A/0x1B are 毒擊術 poison-strike / 麻痹術 paralysis (NOT summon -- summons are 0x20-0x23, unhandled, return 0); 0x15 is 祛麻術 cure paralysis. tally_chars_with_zero_at_field for 0x1A/0x1B counts targets whose status byte is still 0 (un-afflicted), which is correct for an inflict spell. The plate's 'Alt-entry at +0x223' was reworded: 0x15d9a is the function's shared stack-teardown epilogue (ADD ESP,0x10; POP..; RET), into which fd2_wait_for_input_dialog_with_blink jumps to reuse the teardown -- interleaved-code tail sharing, not a separate logical entry point to this scorer. runtime_char HP at +0x40/+0x42 matches the code's actual layout (RUNTIME_CHAR_SIZE 0x50) used consistently across the sibling AI scorers; the KB memory_hack.htm save-layout differs and is not authoritative for runtime access.
